## Overview

Bayesian comparisons of soil carbon decomposition rates, transfer coefficients, and carbon persistence metrics were conducted using posterior distributions obtained from previously fitted three-pool SoilR models for each treatment (Control, Lime, Bolsdorfer, Hühnerberg, and Eifelgold). Posterior parameter samples were extracted from the existing Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) outputs after excluding the first 20,000 iterations as burn-in, with 1,000 posterior draws retained per treatment. The parameters evaluated included the decomposition rates of the fast, intermediate, and slow carbon pools (\(k_f\), \(k_i\), and \(k_s\), respectively), and the transfer coefficients between the fast and intermediate pools (\(\alpha_{fi}\)) and intermediate and slow pools (\(\alpha_{is}\)). For each posterior parameter draw, carbon pool ages and whole-system transit time were derived using the SoilR functions `systemAge()` and `transitTime()`, respectively, with a mean carbon input of 100 and an age grid ranging from 0 to 500 years. This provided posterior distributions for the mean ages of the fast particulate organic matter (fPOM), occluded particulate organic matter (oPOM), and mineral-associated organic matter (MAOM) pools, as well as the overall system transit time.

Treatment effects were evaluated through posterior contrasts between each amendment treatment and the Control, comprising Lime, Hühnerberg (50 t ha\(^{-1}\)), Eifelgold (50 t ha\(^{-1}\)), and Bolsdorfer (50 t ha\(^{-1}\)). For each contrast, 10,000 differences were generated by independently sampling from the corresponding treatment and Control posterior distributions. The median posterior difference and associated 95% credible interval (CrI; 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles) were calculated, together with the posterior probabilities that the treatment value was greater or lower than the Control value. A treatment effect was considered to be supported by the posterior distribution when its 95% CrI did not include zero. Results are presented as forest plots of treatment–Control differences. All comparisons were based on the existing treatment-level SoilR model outputs; consequently, these contrasts quantify differences between treatment-level posterior distributions and do not represent a hierarchical model of plot-level variation.

## Load saved Bayesian results

This document loads the completed RDS object generated by `Malle_SoilR_Bayesian_Treatment_Comparisons.R`. It does not refit the SoilR models, recalculate posterior contrasts, or load previously exported plot images. All figures below are reconstructed directly from the saved posterior comparison results.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(here)
})

results_file <- here::here(
  "outputs",
  "Bayesian_SoilR_Treatment_Comparisons",
  "SoilR_Bayesian_Treatment_Comparison_Complete.rds"
)

if (!file.exists(results_file)) {
  stop(
    "The saved SoilR comparison object was not found at: ",
    results_file,
    "\nRun Malle_SoilR_Bayesian_Treatment_Comparisons.R first."
  )
}

soilR_results <- readRDS(results_file)

if (is.null(soilR_results$primary_contrasts)) {
  stop("The saved RDS object does not contain `primary_contrasts`.")
}

primary_contrasts <- as_tibble(soilR_results$primary_contrasts)

required_columns <- c(
  "Response", "Treatment", "Comparison",
  "Difference_median", "Lower_95", "Upper_95"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(required_columns, names(primary_contrasts))

if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
  stop(
    "The saved primary contrast results are missing required columns: ",
    paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# Retain complete treatment-versus-Control contrasts.
# Standardise treatment names for consistent plotting.

primary_contrasts <- primary_contrasts %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(Difference_median),
    !is.na(Lower_95),
    !is.na(Upper_95)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Treatment = case_when(
      str_detect(str_to_lower(Treatment), "huh|hüh|\\bhb\\b") ~
        "Hühnerberg (50 t ha⁻¹)",
      str_detect(str_to_lower(Treatment), "eifel|\\beg\\b") ~
        "Eifelgold (50 t ha⁻¹)",
      str_detect(str_to_lower(Treatment), "bolsdorfer|\\bbd\\b") ~
        "Bolsdorfer (50 t ha⁻¹)",
      str_detect(str_to_lower(Treatment), "lime") ~ "Lime",
      TRUE ~ Treatment
    ),
    Treatment = factor(
      Treatment,
      levels = c(
        "Lime",
        "Hühnerberg (50 t ha⁻¹)",
        "Eifelgold (50 t ha⁻¹)",
        "Bolsdorfer (50 t ha⁻¹)"
      )
    )
  )

# Response groups.

plot_groups <- list(
  Decomposition_Rates = c("kf", "ki", "ks"),
  Transfer_Coefficients = c("alpha_fi", "alpha_is"),
  Pool_Mean_Ages = c("fPOM_age", "oPOM_age", "MAOM_age"),
  System_Transit_Time = c("system_transit_time")
)

group_titles <- c(
  Decomposition_Rates = "Decomposition rates",
  Transfer_Coefficients = "Transfer coefficients",
  Pool_Mean_Ages = "Mean carbon-pool ages",
  System_Transit_Time = "Whole-system transit time"
)

# Response labels.

response_label <- function(x) {

  labels <- c(
    kf = "Fast-pool decomposition rate (kf)",
    ki = "Intermediate-pool decomposition rate (ki)",
    ks = "Slow-pool decomposition rate (ks)",
    alpha_fi = "Fast-to-intermediate transfer (alpha_fi)",
    alpha_is = "Intermediate-to-slow transfer (alpha_is)",
    fPOM_age = "fPOM mean age",
    oPOM_age = "oPOM mean age",
    MAOM_age = "MAOM mean age",
    system_transit_time = "System transit time"
  )

  unname(labels[x])
}
```

## Primary treatment-versus-Control forest plots

Each point represents the median posterior treatment-minus-Control difference. Horizontal lines show the 95% credible intervals.

**Each response has an independent horizontal axis scale**, allowing responses with substantially different magnitudes (for example, fPOM and MAOM mean ages) to be viewed at an appropriate scale.

Differences are displayed on the original, unstandardised parameter scales:

- Decomposition rates: yr⁻¹
- Transfer coefficients: dimensionless
- Carbon-pool ages: years
- System transit time: years

Differences greater than zero indicate higher values in the amendment treatment than in the Control; differences below zero indicate lower values. Credible intervals that do not cross zero indicate contrasts for which the posterior distribution supports a difference from the Control.

```{r}
#| label: forest-plot-function
#| include: false

make_primary_forest_plot <- function(
    group_name,
    responses,
    x_axis_label
) {

  plot_data <- primary_contrasts %>%
    filter(Response %in% responses) %>%
    mutate(
      Response_label = factor(
        response_label(Response),
        levels = response_label(responses)
      )
    ) %>%
    arrange(Response_label, Treatment)

  if (nrow(plot_data) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(
      y = Treatment,
      x = Difference_median
    )
  ) +

    # Zero reference line.
    geom_vline(
      xintercept = 0,
      linewidth = 0.45,
      linetype = "dashed",
      colour = "grey45"
    ) +

    # 95% credible intervals.
    geom_segment(
      aes(
        x = Lower_95,
        xend = Upper_95,
        y = Treatment,
        yend = Treatment
      ),
      linewidth = 0.65,
      colour = "grey35"
    ) +

    # Posterior median differences.
    geom_point(
      size = 2.5,
      shape = 21,
      stroke = 0.55,
      fill = "black",
      colour = "black"
    ) +

    # IMPORTANT: free_x gives each response its own x-axis scale.
    facet_wrap(
      vars(Response_label),
      ncol = 1,
      scales = "free_x"
    ) +

    labs(
      title = unname(group_titles[group_name]),
      subtitle = paste(
        "Posterior treatment-minus-Control differences",
        "(median and 95% CrI)"
      ),
      x = x_axis_label,
      y = NULL
    ) +

    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +

    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 13
      ),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(
        size = 9.5,
        colour = "grey35"
      ),
      strip.background = element_rect(
        fill = "grey93",
        colour = "grey75"
      ),
      strip.text = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        hjust = 0
      ),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y = element_text(
        colour = "black"
      ),
      axis.title.x = element_text(
        margin = margin(t = 8)
      ),
      panel.spacing = unit(
        0.8,
        "lines"
      ),
      plot.margin = margin(
        8, 12, 8, 8
      )
    )
}
```

### Decomposition rates

```{r}
#| label: forest-decomposition
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7

make_primary_forest_plot(
  group_name = "Decomposition_Rates",
  responses = plot_groups$Decomposition_Rates,
  x_axis_label = paste0(
    "Treatment − Control difference in decomposition rate (yr",
    "\u207B\u00B9",
    ")"
  )
)
```

### Transfer coefficients

```{r}
#| label: forest-transfer
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5.5

make_primary_forest_plot(
  group_name = "Transfer_Coefficients",
  responses = plot_groups$Transfer_Coefficients,
  x_axis_label = paste(
    "Treatment − Control difference in transfer coefficient",
    "(dimensionless)"
  )
)
```

### Mean carbon-pool ages

```{r}
#| label: forest-pool-ages

make_primary_forest_plot(

  responses = plot_groups$Pool_Mean_Ages,
  x_axis_label = paste(
    "Treatment − Control difference in mean pool age (years)"
  )
)
```

### Whole-system transit time

```{r}
#| label: forest-transit-time
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4

make_primary_forest_plot(
  group_name = "System_Transit_Time",
  responses = plot_groups$System_Transit_Time,
  x_axis_label = paste(
    "Treatment − Control difference in system transit time (years)"
  )
)
```
